summary:
The best opportunity this week is new regulatory news that people can search for. Health Canada approved Foundayo (orforglipron) on Nov 13, and Canadian news covered it Nov 18. Australia's medicines regulator (the TGA) cleared it about Nov 17, and pharmacies there should stock it within days. Canadian pharmacies get it in January. That lines up with our Foundayo "what to expect" long video, which is already gaining about 49 minutes a day. Also new: on Nov 18 Health Canada approved Mounjaro to lower heart-attack and stroke risk, based on the SURPASS-CVOT trial against Trulicity. That gives us an approved-drug head-to-head and a label change in one broad "tirzepatide and your heart" video.

Thanksgiving peaks in 7 days. UCLA Health published a GLP-1 holiday guide on Nov 18, so the 20:00 holiday-table Shorts are well timed. The FDA's eye warning (NAION) is still in the news (a Moran Eye Center piece and a MedPage Today opinion, both Nov 18). It's peaking, so use it in the Serious Risks video and calm Shorts, not as a new long video. The Washington Post and The Independent ran "lift weights on a GLP-1" stories on Nov 18. That suits Shorts, but leave the Strength long video alone until 11-24.

The children and teen trials (STEP Young, SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS) are everywhere in mainstream news but fit our adult audience poorly. The GLP-1 "brain" headlines come from a Science review, and the semaglutide Alzheimer's trials (EVOKE) failed, so that story only works as a myth correction.

Rejected: the two case reports of psychosis after stopping tirzepatide (fear bait with only 2 patients), stories on Medicaid, pricing and subscriptions, retatrutide "supplier" ads, and the "low-dose persistence" story (about doses).

The evergreen search formats (felt symptoms, pen how-to, timelines, trial results, stopping) all come from the playbook queue and refresh their search hooks this week.

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) pill: what to expect, now approved in Canada (Nov 13) and Australia (TGA, mid-Nov), from the label only
candidates.angle: Tirzepatide's maker now has a daily GLP-1 pill that more countries have approved. What the label says to expect in the first weeks: who it's approved for, the common GI effects and how they usually ease, and how the pill differs from a weekly shot. Use label figures only: top label dose 17.2 mg, −11.1% in Trial 1; the 36 mg and −11.2% figures are trial-only. No prices, no buying info. Ships as queue item 4 (regenerate the broken 11-11 audio scene, fix masking and the cut-off description). Add a short CA/AU availability line, and link it to How It Works.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–14 days (Australian pharmacy launch within days, Canadian pharmacies in January)
candidates.why_now: Health Canada (Nov 13, covered by CTV Nov 18) and the TGA have just approved it. That opens new search demand in two of our four core markets. Our existing Foundayo video already gains about 49 minutes a day from 'foundayo' searches. Creator coverage outside the US is still thin.

evidence.signal: Health Canada authorized Foundayo Nov 13 for adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, and for type 2 diabetes. Pharmacies expected in January.
TGA approves Foundayo; expected in pharmacies within days
'New oral GLP-1 to hit Australian shelves within days' (Nov 17)
New review comparing the safety and tolerability of oral small-molecule vs injectable GLP-1 drugs (Nov 16). Use as a supporting chapter only.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and your heart: SURPASS-CVOT head-to-head vs dulaglutide (Trulicity). Health Canada approved the heart-risk indication on Nov 18 (FDA in Aug 2026).
candidates.angle: Broad searched question: 'Does tirzepatide protect your heart?' Answer from the label and the trial. 13,000+ adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease, followed about 4.5 years. 8% lower rate of heart death, heart attack or stroke vs Trulicity, HR 0.92 (95.3% CI 0.83–1.01). Say plainly that this was a non-inferiority result against another active drug, not a placebo, and that the approval covers only that population. Weight-loss trials make a separate chapter. Link to Side Effects.
candidates.why_now: New approval in Canada (Nov 18) on top of the recent FDA label update. It's the first head-to-head heart-outcomes trial between two incretin medicines, and it fills our 'benefits beyond weight' pillar. Few creators have explained the head-to-head design.

evidence.signal: Health Canada notice of compliance Nov 18. 8% lower MACE vs Trulicity, HR 0.92 (0.83–1.01), 13,000+ participants
FDA approved Mounjaro to lower heart attack and stroke risk in adults with T2D
Meta-analysis of RCTs on GLP-1-based therapies, heart failure and cardiovascular outcomes (Nov 13)

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: full after 3 bites, heartburn after the big plate, greasy food, drinks at the party, leftovers
candidates.angle: 20:00 holiday-table Shorts. Make each one a felt moment ('full after three bites, is that normal?'). Relief line first, then one rounded number at most. Practical help from the label: smaller portions, eat slowly, stop when full, go easy on greasy food. Every Short targets the Thanksgiving long video.
keywords: full after a few bites mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Thanksgiving is Nov 26. UCLA Health published a GLP-1 Thanksgiving guide on Nov 18, and FoodNavigator is covering GLP-1s at Christmas. It has appeared in 7 straight snapshots at momentum 88–90.

evidence.signal: Thanksgiving on a GLP-1: nutritionist tips (Nov 18)
How GLP-1s could change Christmas eating (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Travelling with your tirzepatide pen over Thanksgiving: storage and carrying, from the Instructions for Use
candidates.angle: Device how-to Short for 08:00 or 20:00. Name the device. The single-dose pen and the vial can stay unrefrigerated (up to 86°F) for up to 21 days total. KwikPens have different limits. Explain how to keep it from getting too hot or freezing. Cite the real IFU URL only. Target: Pen how-to.
keywords: how long can zepbound be unrefrigerated
candidates.why_now: Holiday travel week is coming. Device how-tos beat our usual views by 10–195x in this niche, and our pen Shorts are among the winners (pen blood 132 on YouTube, 641 on TikTok).

evidence.signal: Seen in 3 snapshots, momentum rising 78→81
Holiday GLP-1 coverage peaking this week

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) weight loss: how much in the trials? SURMOUNT-1 averages by arm in the full trial population
candidates.angle: Queue item 3. Give both arms, with the full population named: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. Explain why results vary. State the 75/25 fat-to-lean split only with its scope (160-person DXA substudy). Fix the known faults first: re-time from final word timestamps, the pinned-comment population, the watch-next target. The fresh hook is a real-world tirzepatide effectiveness paper (Diabetes & Metabolism, Nov 12), used only as context.
keywords: how much weight can you lose on mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; surges in the New Year resolution window (late Dec–Jan)
candidates.why_now: One of the most-searched broad questions. It has risen across 4 snapshots (80→84), and a new real-world effectiveness paper gives a fresh hook ahead of January.

evidence.signal: Real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in obesity: weight response, treatment factors, diabetes status (Nov 12)
Update on new tirzepatide studies and pre-specified analyses

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your eyes: the FDA's class-wide NAION warning, how rare it is (about 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years), and what symptoms mean urgent care
candidates.angle: Label-change format, told calmly. The relief comes before any fear word: it's rare. Then the one symptom to act on: sudden, painless vision loss in one eye means urgent care. Then questions to bring to your prescriber. Name both NANOS and the AAO if cited. Use it as a chapter in the queued 'Serious Risks: How Rare?' long video, plus one 'Is this normal?' Short. No standalone long video, since the topic is peaking.
candidates.why_now: Second-wave coverage on Nov 18: University of Utah Moran Eye Center, a MedPage Today opinion, Newswise and Men's Journal. Fearful headlines are spreading, so a calm explainer stands out. Our NAION TikTok reached 439.

evidence.signal: FDA to require NAION warning for all GLP-1 therapies (Nov 9)
126 trials, 134,000+ patients: 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 per year
Moran Eye Center physician helped inform the FDA warnings (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Lifting weights on tirzepatide: it's about strength and function, not only muscle mass (T-REx RCT, Nature Medicine, Nov 9)
candidates.angle: Shorts only until Exp E ends on 11-24 (don't touch the Strength long video). Answer the 'why lift if muscle loss is overblown?' angle from the Washington Post and Independent: in T-REx, strength went up instead of down. One rounded number per sentence. Target: the Strength long video after 11-24, otherwise Side Effects.
keywords: how to keep muscle on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post and The Independent both ran the story on Nov 18, it has appeared in 7 snapshots, and the New Year gym season is coming.

evidence.signal: 'Lifting weights on a GLP-1 is critical — but not because it saves muscle' (Nov 18)
Why you need to hit the weights on a GLP-1 (Nov 18)
Navigating GLP-1 therapy in sarcopenic obesity (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions and pen moments: redness, itching, a small lump, a drop of blood. Is this normal?
candidates.angle: 08:00 'Is this normal?' Short, the proven winner format. Label figures: injection-site reactions in 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo. Relief first, then the IFU steps (rotate sites, which areas are approved), then when to call. Target: Pen how-to.
keywords: red itchy spot after mounjaro shot
candidates.why_now: Proven winner: injection site Shorts reached 254 and 204, and the pen-blood Short 132 on YouTube and 641 on TikTok. Six snapshots with steady demand, and new starters arrive every week.

evidence.signal: Scoping review of adverse effects reported in semaglutide RCTs (Nov 14). Shows ongoing interest in side effects; for tirzepatide, cite the label.
'Tirzepatide long-term side effects' consumer content ranking this week

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: why it's more common in women (label: 5.4% vs 0.9%; women 7.1%, men 0.5%) and whether it grows back
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Short, plus the retitle of the Hair Loss long video ('Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Hair Loss: Why More in Women?'). Explain that hair shedding can follow rapid weight loss, and protein's role, without overclaiming. A new US survey on skin and hair effects of GLP-1 weight loss is context only, never the topic. Target: Hair Loss.
keywords: does hair grow back after mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Our biggest Short ever (hair grow-back, 1,025), and hair in women reached 119. A new dermatology survey adds a fresh mention.

evidence.signal: US survey of skin and hair effects and quality of life with GLP-1 weight loss (observational: context only)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea: why it happens, when it usually eases (mostly during dose escalation, decreasing over time) and what helps
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Shorts that point to the Nausea Foods long video. Avoid any 'go up slower' advice: a titration RCT protocol (TiTRE) exists, but it is a protocol, not results, and titration is the prescriber's call. Practical help only: smaller meals, eat slowly, avoid greasy food, fluids.
candidates.why_now: Proven Short (191), appearing in 6 snapshots, and the holiday-meal context makes it timely. A new randomized trial protocol on side-effect titration shows clinical interest.

evidence.signal: TiTRE RCT protocol on reducing tirzepatide side effects (Nov 16; protocol only, no results)

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: what SURMOUNT-4 shows (335 vs 335; +14.0% regain on placebo, still 9.9% below baseline)
candidates.angle: Shorts and a pinned-comment refresh that point to Stopping and Keeping Results. Tell it only through the trials, and always pair it with 'don't stop or change your medicine without your prescriber.' Men's Fitness and local clinics are covering 'coming off' this week. Do NOT use the psychosis case reports.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Appears in several snapshots (momentum 80–88). New consumer coverage this week (Men's Fitness Nov 17, WBOC clinic guidance Nov 18). Our Stopping video has a 5.68% CTR.

evidence.signal: 'Can you keep the weight off after you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide?' (Nov 17)
Clinic guidance for patients coming off semaglutide (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) months 2–6 and first month: what to expect, from the label and trial averages
candidates.angle: Timeline-format Shorts ('Month 3 on tirzepatide: is this normal?') that feed the new series playlist 'Your First Months on Tirzepatide'. GI effects came mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time; appetite and food noise; pace of loss as trial averages. No dose steps. Target: Months 2–6.
candidates.why_now: 'What to expect' timelines are a 10–195x search format. Months 2–6 went live 11-16 and needs Shorts pointing to it. New 'starting a GLP-1' coverage this week (WFAA, Nov 18).

evidence.signal: 'What should you consider when starting GLP-1 drugs?' (Nov 18)
Real-world body-composition path in early tirzepatide treatment (context only)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide: which works better? The approved head-to-head (SURMOUNT-5), with the GLP1R gene-variant study as context
candidates.angle: Approved-drug head-to-head against tirzepatide, a 10x search format. Lead with SURMOUNT-5 (randomized, adults with obesity without diabetes, full population named). Then the Nature Metabolism variant finding as a 'why one may work differently for some people' context chapter: genetics, early research, no testing advice. Never advise switching. Title: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) vs Semaglutide: Which Works Better?'
keywords: which is better mounjaro or ozempic
candidates.why_now: The GLP1R variant story is still spreading (AllSci, Nov 16). Real-world switching data (Medical Daily, Nov 16) and new observational tirzepatide-vs-semaglutide heart papers keep the comparison in the news. Evergreen search demand is high.

evidence.signal: Rare GLP-1 receptor variants linked to weaker semaglutide response but not tirzepatide (Nov 16)
Semaglutide vs tirzepatide heart outcomes, target trial emulation (observational: context only)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide serious risks: how rare are they? Pancreatitis, gallbladder, low blood sugar, NAION, from the label
candidates.angle: Queue item 6 (apply the 11-14 REVISE fixes). Hook it to 'tirzepatide long-term side effects' searches. A Surg Endosc observational paper (GLP-1 use linked to more severe pancreatitis) and FAERS reports on aspiration and GI slowing are in the news. Mention them only as 'what researchers are watching', never as the topic. Label numbers: pancreatitis 0.14 vs 0.15 per 100 years in weight trials, alongside the diabetes pool. Low-blood-sugar risk applies only to people on insulin or a sulfonylurea.
candidates.why_now: Safety news cluster this week: AHCJ 'GLP-1 safety' (Nov 18), the NAION second wave, and new pancreatitis and pharmacovigilance papers. Ro's 'long-term side effects' page shows search demand.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 use associated with higher acute-pancreatitis severity (observational, Nov 17)
FAERS analysis of perioperative aspiration reports (Nov 17)
'Get the skinny on GLP-1 safety' (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Food noise and binge eating on GLP-1 medicines: 60-week semaglutide RCT (Int J Eat Disord) plus new clinical guidance on GLP-1s and eating disorders
candidates.angle: Food-noise pillar, told with care. A 60-week placebo-controlled RCT found semaglutide reduced binge-eating symptoms and body dissatisfaction. Keep it semaglutide-only, and name the BMI >27 population. Pair it with the new guidance: eating disorders need specialist care, and the drug isn't an eating-disorder treatment. No restriction messaging. Best as a chapter or a carefully worded Short.
candidates.why_now: An RCT plus guidance from Medical Xpress and the AAMC, all covered Nov 17–18. Food Noise is one of our top long videos (476 minutes).

evidence.signal: 60-week randomized placebo-controlled trial of semaglutide on disordered eating, BMI >27
New guidance on GLP-1 use and eating disorders (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide affect your brain? What the new Science review says, and why semaglutide didn't slow early Alzheimer's (EVOKE)
candidates.angle: Myth-correction, positive tone. GLP-1 receptors in the brain explain appetite and food noise (well supported). Dementia links come from observational data only. The EVOKE/EVOKE+ trials of semaglutide failed to slow early Alzheimer's. The honest takeaway: 'promising, unproven.' Fits as a chapter in How It Works, or one Short.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily (Nov 17) and Medical Daily (Nov 18) are amplifying a Science review. 'Surprising effect on your brain' headlines invite misreading, so there's room for a clear correction.

evidence.signal: Science review: observational dementia link; EVOKE trials negative; trials needed
Semaglutide did not slow early Alzheimer's in two major trials (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your kidneys: new trial-level meta-analysis across albuminuria, filtration and clinical outcomes
candidates.angle: Benefits-beyond-weight pillar. Pairs with the heart video as a 'what tirzepatide does beyond the scale' chapter. Keep it to what the pooled trials show, and name the populations (mostly type 2 diabetes). Semaglutide's FLOW is the approved kidney-outcome trial, for contrast.
candidates.why_now: A new meta-analysis (Nov 13) and FLOW post hoc analyses (Nov 18), with almost no consumer coverage yet.

evidence.signal: Parent-trial-level meta-analysis of tirzepatide kidney effects (Nov 13)

evidence.source: PubMed / Clin J Am Soc Nephrol
evidence.signal: FLOW post hoc analyses across racial and ethnic groups (Nov 18)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines in children and teens: STEP Young (semaglutide, ages 6–11, NEJM) and SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (tirzepatide, JAMA)
candidates.angle: Low audience fit (we serve adults). If covered at all: one calm parent-focused Short or chapter, with exact populations and results, side effects (vomiting common), and that weight rose after stopping in STEP Young. No 'should kids take it' advocacy; it's the pediatrician's call.
candidates.why_now: Saturated mainstream coverage (NYT, ABC, CNBC, NY Post) since Nov 16. Late for us, and outside our core audience.

evidence.signal: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS randomized trial
Semaglutide in children 6 to <12 (STEP Young)

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'psychosis or mania after abruptly stopping GLP-1s' (2 case reports), plus Medicaid, pricing and subscription stories, retatrutide 'supplier' ads, and the 'low-dose persistence' story
candidates.angle: Don't produce. Two case reports are anecdotes that invite fear-mongering and could prompt unsafe behaviour. Pricing, Medicaid and pharmacy topics are banned. Retatrutide supplier pieces promote gray-market sources. The dose-persistence story leads into dosing territory. If a viewer asks about stopping, point them to the Stopping video and their prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Present in today's feed. Logged so downstream agents skip it.

evidence.source: Primary Care Companion for CNS Disorders
evidence.signal: Two case reports of mood and psychotic symptoms after rapidly stopping tirzepatide
Retatrutide 'supplier' promotion (gray market)
